subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: Should OpenClaw add a core global agent dry-run mode, and which execution surfaces must be covered before users can trust it as a safety boundary?
rationale: Automation can prove the current gap, but it cannot choose whether adapter-only interception is acceptable or whether Gateway, client-hosted, and external runtime tool paths must be included from day one.

options.title: Design the safety contract first
options.body: Specify covered surfaces, preview/result shape, and unsupported/bypass behavior, then implement only that explicit mode with side-effect proof.

options.title: Fold into broader safe modes
options.body: Track this as the tool-call preview requirement under the broader Ask/Plan/Modify or scoped-execution product direction.

options.title: Decline global interception
options.body: Keep per-command dry-runs and tool policy hooks as the supported safety tools, then close this direction after maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Design the safety contract first
recommendation.body: Specify covered surfaces, preview/result shape, and unsupported/bypass behavior, then implement only that explicit mode with side-effect proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The clearest older history signal on central agent command and execution helper surfaces points to this owner for the product/security contract decision.
